lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eafini:
"

Affinity is the ability to bind; efficacy is the ability to activate the receptor. The full agonist (e = 1) produces the maximum response; the partial one (0 < e < 1) produces a smaller response even when occupying all the receptors; the antagonist (e = 0) binds without activating and blocks the agonist. Change the type of ligand and watch the illuminated receptors.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ecurva:
"

The dose–response curve (response versus log [L]) is a sigmoid. The EC50 is the concentration that produces 50 % of the maximum effect, and measures potency; the Emax measures efficacy. A partial agonist has a lower Emax. With a simple model (no amplification), EC50 = Kd.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara que un fármaco s:
"

For a drug to be absorbed orally, it should meet Lipinski's rule of five: molar mass ≤ 500 g/mol, logP ≤ 5, ≤ 5 H-bond donors and ≤ 10 acceptors. More than one violation predicts poor absorption or permeability. There are exceptions (cyclosporine, natural products). Choose a drug and compare its properties.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eantag:
"

A competitive antagonist competes for the same site. It decreases the occupancy by the agonist: [A]/([A] + Kd(1 + [B]/Kb)). The curve shifts to the right (EC50 increases) but keeps the Emax: it is overcome with more agonist. The shift (dose ratio) is 1 + [B]/Kb (Schild analysis).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003erecep:
"

A receptor is a protein (in the membrane or inside the cell) that recognizes a ligand with high affinity and specificity. Binding is reversible, L + R ⇌ LR, with dissociation constant Kd = [L][R]/[LR]: the lower the Kd, the higher the affinity. The fraction of occupied receptors is [L]/([L] + Kd): 50 % when [L] = Kd.

"
lit.\u0027«Curva dosis–respuesta» (respuesta: '“Dose–response curve” (response versus log [L]) and “Lipinski”, which compares the drug’s properties with the limits for oral use.'
lit.\u0027«Tipo» elige el ligando (agonista: '“Type” picks the ligand (full agonist, partial agonist or antagonist); “log [L]” and “log Kd” set the occupancy = [L]/([L] + Kd); “log [antagonist]” adds a competitor; “Drug” picks the compound for Lipinski.'
lit.\u0027a la derecha, con el mismo Emáx\u0: "to the right, with the same Emax"
lit.\u0027Agrega antagonista: la curva dosis: 'Add antagonist: the dose–response curve shifts to the right but reaches the same Emax.'
lit.\u0027Antagonista competitivo: curva a l: "Competitive antagonist: curve to the right, same Emax."
lit.\u0027Barras: valor del fármaco / límite: "Bars: drug value / limit. Red = exceeds the limit."
lit.\u0027cada cilindro es un receptor y se: 'each cylinder is a receptor and turns yellow when activated; the share of yellow receptors reflects the response.'
lit.\u0027Cada cilindro es un receptor; las: "Each cylinder is a receptor; the green spheres are bound agonists and the red ones, antagonists. A yellow receptor is activated. In “Lipinski” you see the four properties of a drug."
lit.\u0027Cambia a agonista parcial: aunque: 'Switch to a partial agonist: even with every receptor occupied it does not reach the full agonist’s Emax.'
lit.\u0027El antagonista desplaza la curva a: "The antagonist shifts the curve to the right without reducing the Emax"
lit.\u0027esferas verdes = agonista unido; e: 'green spheres = bound agonist; red spheres = bound antagonist (it occupies the receptor without activating it).'
lit.\u0027La eficacia (e) distingue lo que h: "Efficacy (e) distinguishes what the drug does once bound"
lit.\u0027La regla de Lipinski fija como máx: "Lipinski's rule sets as the maximum molar mass…"
lit.\u0027Línea verde: agonista solo. Línea: "Green line: agonist alone. Red line: with antagonist (shifted). Dot: your dose."
lit.\u0027no alcanza el Emáx del completo\u0: "does not reach the Emax of the full one"
lit.\u0027Pon log [L] igual a log Kd: la ocu: 'Set log [L] equal to log Kd: occupancy should be 50 %.'
lit.\u0027Reglas de Lipinski: PM ≤ 500 · log: "Lipinski's rules: MW ≤ 500 · logP ≤ 5 · H donors ≤ 5 · H acceptors ≤ 10"
lit.\u0027Respuesta frente a log[L]: sigmoid: "Response versus log[L]: sigmoid with EC₅₀ at the midpoint"
lit.\u0027Un fármaco se une reversiblemente: "A drug binds reversibly to its receptor: occupancy = [L]/([L] + Kd)"
